description: Echo can only repeat. Narcissus only loves his reflection. Two destinies which never manage to come together, and which give birth to the word narcissism.

hero.hook: She no longer has a voice of her own. He only has eyes for himself. Their meeting is impossible.

blocks.text: The Roman poet  recounts in his  the crossed destiny of **Narcissus** and **Echo**. She is a nymph deprived of her own words. Him, a young man captivated by his image. [[Ovid]] [[Metamorphoses]]
This myth is the direct source of the word **narcissism**. It talks about impossible love, indifference and the trap of only wanting oneself.

Before becoming a simple sound phenomenon, **Echo** is a [[Oread]], mountain nymph, famous for her abundant speech. She helps **Zeus**, king of the gods, to hide his infidelities. While he joins other nymphs, she retains **Hera**, the jealous wife, with endless conversations.

blocks.caption: Echo, condemned to be nothing more than a repeating voice.

blocks.text: When Hera discovers the ruse, she punishes Echo. The nymph can no longer begin a sentence. She can only **repeat the last words** of others. His own desires no longer have a language.
In another version, the god **Bang**, furious at being rejected, has Echo torn to pieces. Ovid's version, where she is consumed with love, has remained the most famous.

**Narcissus** is son of the river god Cephisus and the nymph Liriope. Her beauty attracts everyone. His pride pushes everyone away. The soothsayer **Tirésias** had warned his mother: “He will live to be old if he does not know himself. »

In the woods, Echo sees him and falls in love with him. Unable to speak first, she waits. Narcisse calls: “Is there anyone? » She replies: “Someone! » When she approaches to hug him, he rejects her with contempt.
Humiliated, Echo retreats into the caves. She stops eating. His body withers, his bones become stone. Only a wandering voice remains in the mountains.
Narcissus' cruelty tires the gods. One of his victims prays to , goddess of just revenge: that he loves himself thus and can never possess the object of his love. The wish is granted. [[Nemesis]]

One hot day, Narcissus leans into a clear spring. He uncovers his face. He thinks he sees a water spirit. He falls in love with her. Teiresias' prophecy is fulfilled: in knowing himself, he loses himself.
He tries to kiss the reflection. The water becomes cloudy. Prisoner of this sterile passion, he forgets to eat and drink.
Then comes tragic lucidity: “I am the one I see. » Impossible to unite with oneself. Narcissus is consumed. Echo, faithful despite everything, repeats his last farewell.

When the [[Naiads]], water nymphs, and the [[Dryads]], tree nymphs, come for the funeral, the body has disappeared. In its place grows a flower with a yellow heart and white petals: the **daffodil**, leaning towards the water like the young man towards his image.

In **1914**, **Freud** published “To introduce narcissism”. He describes love turned towards oneself rather than towards the other. The myth becomes a key to modern psychology, and a warning: without a true encounter, all that remains is a voice without a body and a flower without a soul.
**Echo** dies from not being able to express his desire. **Narcissus** perishes for having desired only himself. Two ways of missing the other, one tragedy.
